Style: Long Layered Cut with Face-Framing Pieces
What It Does for a Fuller Face: Layers set up a downward path for the eye so it travels vertically instead of around the cheek curve; framing pieces interrupt the smooth round silhouette
Length Band: Collarbone or longer with the framing pieces landing past the jawline
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Soft layers starting below the chin (eachinstyle.com) - disputed: abodemom.com asks for face-framing layers starting at the cheekbone; both positions stated
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Curtain bangs opening at the centre and sweeping along the cheekbones or side bangs running the eye diagonally; centre or soft off-centre part

What It Does for a Fuller Face: Length below the chin gives the lower face a longer read; cut too short the same shape hits the cheeks and reads wider; choppy ends break the curve
Length Band: Just below the chin through collarbone-grazing
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Subtle layers for body with hidden undercut layers reducing jawline bulk while visible length stays intact; trims every 6-8 weeks (trendcottage.com) or 8-10 weeks for face-framing-layer bobs and lobs (hairaide.com)
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Curtain bangs to open the centre line; or a deep side part letting one side fall forward to partially veil the cheek

What It Does for a Fuller Face: Lift concentrated at the crown reads as vertical height against the width; sides kept close stop the cut from widening the face
Length Band: Sides tapered close to the head; top left substantially longer with visible volume
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Texturizing scissors remove heaviness and build movement through the top; the layered crown suits fine hair because the lift reads as fullness the hair does not have; 4-6 week upkeep band
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Side-swept sections draw the eye to the eyes and cheekbones while the taper keeps the silhouette narrow; a deep side part adds the diagonal without any fringe

Style: Long Pixie / Bixie with Extended Front
What It Does for a Fuller Face: Front pieces at or past the jaw give the frame a vertical path past the widest point of the face; on a thinning crown the swept-over top adds the illusion of volume - the pixie direction for fine or thinning hair
Length Band: Front at jaw level or deliberately extended past the chin; sides grazing the chin in the sleek version
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Point-cut ends so the bottom line never reads blunt; framing pieces start at the cheekbone and graduate down; bixie combines a stacked graduated back with the jaw-length front; upkeep every 4-6 weeks
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Long side-swept bangs from a deep part kept from separating with a dab of pomade; or point-cut curtain bangs; texture cream pressed through piece-y bangs

What It Does for a Fuller Face: Layers lighten the hair and crown height elongates the profile; textured ends prevent bulk at the sides; on curls the uneven layers break the symmetry a fuller face presents as width
Length Band: Medium lengths in shoulder territory; the shaggy lob version keeps length past the chin
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Razored jagged layers through the length with volume placed at the roots; wispy ends taper the face inward; suits fine hair because it manufactures motion; air-dry with texturizing spray
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Wispy curtain bangs or a soft fringe added without shortening the face; curtain fringe standard on the shag build

What It Does for a Fuller Face: Short layers at the crown lengthening into longer tiers build a contoured shape around the face; the wispy see-through fringe and face-framing pieces pull the eye inward
Length Band: Long - the length is maintained through the ends which keeps the vertical lines running
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Disputed start point both stated: 5minutesready.com puts the bottleneck layers starting at the cheekbones; faxhionvibe.com asks for feathery point-cut layers starting at chin length and growing longer toward the back
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Wispy see-through fringe; the layered build works on fine hair because the crown layers add lift while the ends stay light

What It Does for a Fuller Face: Volume concentrated at the top pulls attention up and away from the width of the cheeks; choppy crown layers blended into longer textured lengths underneath
Length Band: Choppy layers at the crown with longer textured lengths underneath
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Modified for a fuller face with face-framing pieces that hit at the jawline to define angles; tapered ends and framing layers do the narrowing work together
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Face-framing pieces standard; sea salt spray brings out the natural texture; minimal styling time is part of this cut's pitch

What It Does for a Fuller Face: The diagonal perimeter runs past the fullest part of the cheeks toward the chin; one side visibly longer breaks the symmetry a fuller face reads as width
Length Band: Longer in the front; shorter and graduated toward the back; the dramatic version puts one side at chin length and the other at jaw length with a hidden undercut beneath the shorter side
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: At least two inches of length difference between front and back for the graduation to read clearly; razored or point-cut ends keep the perimeter from landing as one heavy line
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Side-swept bangs add a second diagonal and soften the cheek line; peekaboo bangs swept across one eye push the asymmetry further; a full fringe would fight the asymmetry so fringe is optional

What It Does for a Fuller Face: The guides split three ways: hairaide.com files it as workable when the hemline lands exactly at the narrowest point of the jaw; abodemom.com and 5minutesready.com file it under caution as widening at chin level; lovelyish.com takes the middle position - blunt ends work just below the chin with curtain bangs
Length Band: At the jaw (hairaide.com) versus just below the chin (lovelyish.com) - the dispute is the length band itself
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: None by definition: zero graduation is the build; precision is the whole product with a fresh trim every 6 weeks and even a half-inch of fringe growth changing the framing
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: The fringe dispute rides along: hairaide.com's French-bob build pairs the blunt line with a full eyebrow-skimming fringe as a deliberate two-line strategy while the same page's FAQ plus abodemom.com and 5minutesready.com hold that a full fringe only widens when cut blunt straight across
